# Asset provenance

The game includes generated assets, user-supplied audio, third-party fonts and
the recorded crowd and character assets listed below. Nothing is downloaded at
build time or at run time.

## Generated by the scripts in `tools/`

| Asset | Generator | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assets/models/zombies/zombie_walker.glb`, `zombie_runner.glb`, `zombie_brute.glb`, `zombie_boss.glb` | `tools/build_zombies.py` | Each sculpted as a signed-distance field from its own proportions, meshed, unwrapped, skinned to the same 18-bone skeleton. Open wounds (one down to the ribs on every kind), torn sleeves and trouser legs and a missing shoe are part of the sculpt. Procedural animation clips per kind: a limping walk lame in either leg (the walker has two such gaits, so four walks), idle, attack, hit and two deaths; the runner's lurching sprint, the heavy gait and the two-fisted blow of the brute and the boss are generated the same way |
| `assets/textures/zombies/zombie_walker_{a,b,c,d,e}.png`, `zombie_runner_{a,b,c}.png`, `zombie_brute_{a,b}.png`, `zombie_boss_a.png` | `tools/build_zombies.py` | Painted skins baked from the sculpts: skin, cloth, blood and grime laid by where the surface is and what it is (768 px for the walker and the runner, 1024 px for the brute and the boss) |
| `assets/models/environment/city_siege.glb` | `tools/build_city.py` | Fortress, gate court, ruined city blocks, wrecks and props |
| `assets/models/weapons/rpg_launcher.glb`, `rocket.glb`, `frag_grenade.glb`, `rotary_gun.glb` | `tools/build_weapons.py` | The shoulder launcher with its loaded round, the round in flight, the hand grenade, and the six-barrel gun on its pedestal (a rotor of six barrels that turns, its housing, ammunition can and feed chute), built from lathed and boxed primitives |
| `resources/levels/city_siege_layout.tres` | `tools/build_city.py` | Routes and attack places, from the same numbers as the mesh |
| `assets/textures/world/*.jpg`, `*_n.png`, `sky_dusk.jpg` | `tools/build_textures.py` | Tiling surfaces with normal maps, and the sky panorama |
| `assets/audio/*.wav` (synthesized clips) | `tools/build_audio.py` | Synthesized from oscillators and filtered noise: the guns and the tail of a burst, the six-barrel gun's motor running up, its paired report and its run-down, strikes, voices, the rocket launch, both explosions, the boss's roar and death, a body falling, the interface sounds, the victory and defeat stings, and the wind bed |
| `assets/textures/icon.png` | `tools/build_icon.py` | App icon derived from the generated shield emblem |

## Generated branding artwork

The shield emblem (`assets/textures/branding/emblem.png`) and city loading art
(`assets/textures/branding/loading_city.png`) were generated for this project
with Arena's image generation tool. The app icon is derived from the emblem.
The menu character artwork (`assets/textures/branding/menu_scene.png`) and
tactical map background (`assets/textures/branding/campaign_map.png`) were
also generated for this project using Arena's image generation tool; the
user-provided reference screenshots are not included in the game.

## Licence of the original assets

The earlier project's notes dedicated its original assets to the public
domain (CC0) where legally possible. That text was removed together with the
old documentation; nothing in this pass changes or extends it. Which licence
the new original assets carry is the project owner's decision.

## Engine

Godot Engine 4.7.2, MIT licence. The exported game includes the engine and
its third-party components under their own licences, as listed in Godot's
`COPYRIGHT.txt`.

## Free zombie characters

| Asset | Origin | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assets/models/zombies/zombie_bloat.glb` | `13899_open3dmodel.zip` (Bloat_Summer, free personal-use character from Open3DModel) | Skinned to the shared 18-bone skeleton and mixed into walker, runner and brute spawns. The fat figure has more health than the type's own look. |
| `assets/models/zombies/zombie_boomer.glb` | Same free Bloat mesh, retargeted; colour from the Boomer pack (`27189`, Max-only mesh) | Heavier silhouette, cooler grey-blue skin. |
| `assets/models/zombies/zombie_gibberling.glb` | Same free Bloat mesh, retargeted; colour from the Gibberling pack (`28069`, Max-only mesh) | Narrower hunched figure. |

The Max scenes in `27189_open3dmodel.rar` and `28069_open3dmodel.rar` stay in
the repository root as source; the game loads the converted GLBs.

## Reference material in the repository root

The `.max` file, `.dds` files and character archives in the repository root
are source materials supplied for the project. The game does not load them at
run time; the extra character meshes are converted copies under
`assets/models/zombies/`. Former visual reference images remain in Git history.

## User-supplied packs reviewed

- `Universal_Animation_LibraryStandard.zip`: Quaternius, CC0 1.0. The
  `Hit_Chest` and `Hit_Head` upper-body rotations were retargeted and blended
  into the four original zombie GLBs using `tools/retarget_hits.py`. The
  original model and animation library are not loaded at runtime.
- `Starter-Kit-FPS-main.zip`: Kenney; assets CC0 1.0, code MIT (the archive
  carries a 2025 MIT notice, the README a 2026 notice). The weapon-change
  sound is used as a quiet layer. Its stylized models and moving-player
  controller do not fit the game's stationary realistic gunner.
- `pyrolux_lite_store_v1.0.3.zip`: gennai, free for games but restrictions
  prohibit sharing the effects on their own or in asset packs. Its shaders and
  code have not been copied into the public project; an exported game is
  allowed under its licence. The existing pooled, quality-scaled effects stay
  in place pending a suitable distribution and performance review.

## Recorded combat and creature audio

The local source recordings under `tools/audio_sources/` are CC0 1.0 and are
excluded from Godot import/export by `.gdignore`. `tools/build_audio.py`
downmixes, resamples to 24 kHz mono and peak-normalizes them, with pitch and
short fades. The boss voices use slowed zombie vocals; the rotary report
layers two shortened rifle transients 40 ms apart. The motor and some tails
remain synthesized. No source assets are fetched during a rebuild.

- `zombie_near`, `zombie_attack`, `zombie_die`: artisticdude's [Zombies Sound
  Pack](https://opengameart.org/content/zombies-sound-pack), via
  [Shadow Zombie](https://github.com/Bristy-Mony/Shadow-Zombie-Survival-Game/tree/main/public/assets/audio).
- `zombie_distress`, `zombie_scream`: zombie-12 and zombie-17 from the same
  pack, via [Cornfield](https://github.com/OsanGen/cornfields/blob/main/assets/audio/sources.json).
- `rifle_shot`: AK-47 near recording from [The Free Firearm Sound Library](https://opengameart.org/content/the-free-firearm-sound-library).
- `field_blast`, `firework_blast`: rubberduck's [25 CC0 bang / firework SFX](https://opengameart.org/content/25-cc0-bang-firework-sfx).
  These and the rifle clip are pre-cut/mastered recordings from
  [smokeem](https://github.com/mrellcrane/smokeem/tree/claude/smoke-em-design-setup-ftlkqp/src/audio/samples);
  its explosion clips also include synthesized sub-bass. The game further
  resamples and adjusts them as above.

## Machine-gun surface finish

`assets/textures/weapons/gunmetal.png` is an original procedural, seeded
brushed-metal modulation generated by `tools/build_weapon_finish.py`; no
external textures are used. It is shared by the machine-gun materials.
